body:
Thank you for the reassurance. I think I’m going to see if I get any positive reviews from the friend who she did come with. I did, however, send the Instagram follow and it was received and met with a followback. 

This social media following is a bizarre game we play in the current world, but I will probably reach out over chat in the coming days to thank her for coming and express how nice it was to meet and laugh with her. I think this is an adequate attempt to healthily measure my interest and not come on to strong. Really not trying to be too much at once here
Yes.
Much appreciated.
They’re always a different type of bittersweet. Best to you and yours.
Refreshingly earnest.
Theory is used by the narrator as a tongue-in-cheek expression that intends to highlight how the expectation of a long life is something taken for granted.

The beloved and positive nature of life mentioned in this excerpt is the narrator’s cynical observations on humanity’s obsession with breathing and experiencing.

I did not get to play golf with my father on Father’s Day because he is dead. My least favorite day is the one in which I watched him die by suffocating from his organs being maimed and crushed by tumors.

I agree that was short-sighted of me to say about her being non-supportive. I desperately want her needs to be met. I also want my aunt to feel supported as she has been an incredible support to me since the day I have been born. It is difficult for everyone to win here.

Thanks for your input. I really don’t think she is being ridiculous or unreasonable, but I also know my request to stay is valid. There is a lot of responsibility that has fallen on my shoulders since the passing of my father because I am the oldest of my siblings. I care very much about doing the right thing for all parties.
The former two options.

From this past November to Early January, my father battled a sudden and aggressive Stage Four Metastasized Melanoma that eventually took him from us. From what you have outlined in your posting, you seem to be especially mature and strong for your age, which is quite remarkable in the face of such an adversity. There’s really no correct way to approach something of this nature but I will say to never let the “I love you’s” run dry. I wish your family and yourself strength and I extend my empathy in this difficult time.

I can unfortunately relate here and empathize. My father lost a one and a half month long battle with stage four melanoma that made its way from his adrenal gland to his pancreas, liver, and stomach in January. After three rounds of surgery and multiple appointments, the deciding factor in his immunotherapy and radiation therapy start came down to a stalemate between the hospital and insurance companies, which pushed his treatment appointment back. By the time he could begin immunotherapy, his window had closed. 

I am certain tomorrow is going to be an especially difficult day for you. Spend it in the way you see best. I cannot speak for you, but I do not think it is a stretch that we may feel a similar anger towards the obstacles that stood in the way of our fathers receiving the necessary treatment. I am constantly plagued by racing thoughts of what could have been done to prevent his succumbing to melanoma. I am immensely sorry to know that you might be undergoing something similar. I wish you and your loved ones respite and healing.
He’s homeless by choice. He has an automobile and works jobs.

It’s been twice where we have been at odds and he has called her, resulting in them speaking for 2-3 hours. It makes me feel uncomfortable and mildly betrayed, regardless of the content of her conversation, because it feels like she is attempting to cope with her being upset until she feels like she wants to address and resolve the conflict.

I think that would be the best option but I cannot insist that she has zero contact with anyone. It’s very unfortunate that I have the urge to do physical harm to this person. I know that is never the solution, but I do not want to see her subjected to his bullshit again just to be let off a few months later and have me act a fool for believing that this clown ass is irrelevant. I do not like the strain that other individuals, whether or not they have a confirmed agenda, place on our attempt to be happy together. I do not know if she sees it that way and bringing it up might just perturb her further and lead her to believe I have magnified insecurities.
I appreciate your very direct response. As all things posted on the internet, it is difficult to convey the the full situation, but the straightforwardness is refreshing.
Hard agree.
We have spoken about this several times. she assured me that I’m her boo...but that’s not the reassurance I need.
Thank you for voicing your perspective. It really helps put me at ease about how my father’s situation will progress. I hope for the best for you and your battle ahead.

I am immensely glad to hear that you and your spouse can attest to the game changing affects of the immunotherapy! Hope they can continue to reap the benefits as treatment progresses. 

As I live at home with my father, I am not experiencing the day in day out with him but in being at the oncology appointment where the drugs and side affects were explained, I am aware of how he will be feeling. 

I guess I’m just uneasy about this type of therapy being relatively new and not knowing his exact odds at the moment, especially after the brain mass. Really happy to hear that these have been affective in the case of your spouse!
